news.originalContent:

An Arizona mom has spoken out about the horror of having her toddler pronounced dead, only to learn he was still alive inside a hospital morgue hours after she was forced to bid him a premature farewell.

Alexus Fiordilino told ABC 15 in a sit-down interview on Monday that Feb. 8 was the worst day of her life after finding her 18-month-old boy, Vincent, floating face down in the pool at her Gilbert, Ariz., home.

“I had to say goodbye,” she said, adding “do you know how hard that is?”

Five hours after he was found, the tot was pronounced dead — only to be discovered alive in the morgue when a medical examiner’s transport arrived at the hospital.

“He ended up in the morgue,” Alexus told the outlet.

He suffered serious brain damage and will require assistance for the rest of his life, ABC reported.

When her son arrived at the emergency room following the near-drowning, Fiordilino says that doctors at the hospital told her that even if he was resuscitated, his life would never be the same.

“He comes back, like maybe not even five, 10 minutes later and he’s like ‘yeah so it’s pH levels are too high,” she said of Dr. Aryan Toosi.

“They’re too acidic. So even if we are to bring him back, it wouldn’t be a good form of life,” the doctor reportedly said.

“‘He’d be suffering. So I think it’s best that I call the time for it.’”

Fiordilino says that her son was ice cold when doctors were trying to save him.

“He was so cold,” she said.

“I remember feeling him and being like, ‘he’s so cold.’”

Fiordilino said the toddler was initially breathing in the hospital room before he was erroneously pronounced dead — but hospital staff dismissed it as agonal breathing.

Fiordilino said her mother-in-law noticed signs on life.

“’She’s like, ‘Hey, it sounds like he’s breathing.’ And I’m like, ‘What?”‘ Fiordilino told the ABC 15.

Hospital staff told her that “it’s normal that it’s going to sound like that” and that the breathing was a result of the child’s deoxygenated brain stem, she recalled.

A police report obtained by the Daily Mail allegedly shows that an officer at one point heard a nurse say “I have a pulse” and that other staff moved quickly to help her “in attempting to revive Vincent.”

When the officer told Fiordilino her son had a pulse, Dr. Toosi reportedly brushed him off, stating “he was the doctor, he has a medical degree, he went to medical school for a reason and let him do his thing,” according to the police report.

Six minutes later, Vincent was declared dead.

The cop noted Vincent’s “stomach and chest area was rising and falling” and that she “observed what appeared to be another audible gasp.”

“I again observed what appeared to be a gasp or air release, which was now almost an hour later,” she said, according to the Daily Mail.

After the horrific blunder came to light, Dr. Toosi’s team rushed the boy via emergency airlift to Phoenix Children’s Hospital.

Doctors later determined the child suffered severe brain damage that will leave him cognitively impaired for life.

“He was alone,” said Alexus.

“He was alone for five-and-a-half hours. How do you do that to a baby?”

A representative for Dignity Health told ABC that “out of respect for the patient’s privacy, we cannot share any information and we are unable to comment on those involved in patient care.”

“Patient Safety and exceptional care are our highest priorities.”

A lawyer for Dr. Toosi told the Daily Mail that “his commitment to delivering high-quality care has always been rooted in a desire to provide healing, safety and comfort to his community.”

“Due to pending litigation and privacy laws, we cannot speak to the details of the care provided at this time.”

Gilbert Police Sgt. Jordan Tuckenbrod told the Daily Mail that “the facts gathered in our investigation, combined with all facts known at this time, did not establish probable cause for any criminal conduct involving medical personnel.”

“As a result, no charges were forwarded against those involved.”

“This case is now in the process of being referred to the Attorney General’s Office for their review,” he added.

“We do not have an estimated timeline for when their review would be completed.”
news.content:
پوشش بیشتر ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود ببینید. یک مادر اهل آریزونا درباره وحشت از اعلام مرگ فرزند نوپایش صحبت کرده است، اما ساعاتی پس از آنکه مجبور شد با او خداحافظی زودهنگامی داشته باشد، متوجه شد که او هنوز در سردخانه بیمارستان زنده است. الکسوس فیوردیلینو روز دوشنبه در مصاحبه‌ای با ABC 15 در تاریخ 24 فوریه گفت. روز هشتم بدترین روز زندگی او بود، بعد از اینکه پسر ۱۸ ماهه‌اش، وینسنت، را در حالی که با صورت در استخر خانه‌اش در گیلبرت، آریزونا، شناور بود، پیدا کرد. او گفت: «باید خداحافظی می‌کردم.» و اضافه کرد: «می‌دونی چقدر سخته؟»
 پنج ساعت پس از پیدا شدن، مرگ کودک اعلام شد - اما وقتی تیم پزشکی قانونی به بیمارستان رسید، او را زنده در سردخانه پیدا کردند. الکسوس به این رسانه گفت: «او در نهایت به سردخانه منتقل شد.» به گزارش ای‌بی‌سی، او دچار آسیب مغزی جدی شده و تا آخر عمر به کمک نیاز خواهد داشت. فیوردیلینو می‌گوید وقتی پسرش پس از غرق شدن به اورژانس رسید، پزشکان بیمارستان به او گفتند که حتی اگر احیا شود، زندگی‌اش هرگز مثل قبل نخواهد شد. او در مورد دکتر آریان طوسی گفت: «او برمی‌گردد، شاید حتی پنج یا ده دقیقه بعد هم نباشد و می‌گوید "بله، پس سطح pH خیلی بالاست."» بنا به گزارش‌ها، پزشک گفته است: «آنها خیلی اسیدی هستند. بنابراین حتی اگر قرار باشد او را برگردانیم، این شکل خوبی از زندگی نخواهد بود. او رنج خواهد برد. بنابراین فکر می‌کنم بهتر است که زمان آن فرا برسد.»
 فیوردیلینو می‌گوید وقتی پزشکان سعی داشتند پسرش را نجات دهند، بدنش یخ زده بود. او گفت: «او خیلی سردش بود.»

Don’t bet much on word that Russia is “ready in principle” to resume three-way peace talks with Ukraine and the United States next month; after all, thugocrat Vladimir Putin has been ready to end the war since the day he started it . . . as long as his victim surrenders.

Maybe, just maybe, Moscow is signaling something positive, since that statement emerged after presidential envoy Steve Witkoff briefed Putin on the latest US ceasefire proposals, which he’d already cleared with Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky and other allies at an Oslo sitdown the day before.

Indeed, Zelensky announced he’ll accept a cease-fire that freezes current lines in place, allowing Russia to continue occupying vast swathes of his nation.

On the other hand, Putin’s made plenty of ready-to-talk noises before, only to then demand unilateral concessions before any actual sitdown.

And his Witkoff sitdown looked mostly like a show of politeness that will likely mainly be remembered for Witkoff’s laughably unctuous gush about Putin being a “humanitarian.”

Meanwhile, other Russian officials passed word that Ukraine must make “necessary decisions” or see its situation grow “worse.”

Pretty meager payback, after President Donald Trump first agreed to let Moscow sell millions of barrels of diesel at market prices, end-running sanctions, and then waived fresh sanctions he’d just signed into law.

The Kremlin made one small positive step, releasing American hostage Stephen Hubbard — whom Russian troops seized at age 70 in eastern Ukraine in the second month of the invasion.

Hubbard might visit the White House next week, depending on his condition after years of torture and starvation in Russian prisons.

Trump can take some pride in adding yet another freed hostage to his record total, and maybe his moves will finally pay off in Putin at last agreeing to a cease-fire.

More likely, Vlad will instead try to inflict the worst round of winter suffering yet on Ukraine’s civilians to see if that will break Kyiv; that’s the kind of “humanitarian” he is.
news.content:
پوشش خبری بیشتر ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود ببینید. زیاد روی این حرف که روسیه «از نظر اصولی آماده» است تا مذاکرات صلح سه جانبه با اوکراین و ایالات متحده را ماه آینده از سر بگیرد، شرط نبندید؛ هرچه باشد، ولادیمیر پوتینِ آدمکش از روزی که جنگ را آغاز کرد، آماده پایان دادن به آن بوده است... البته تا زمانی که قربانی‌اش تسلیم شود. شاید، فقط شاید، مسکو در حال نشان دادن نکته مثبتی است، زیرا این بیانیه پس از آن منتشر شد که استیو ویتکوف، فرستاده رئیس جمهور، پوتین را در مورد آخرین پیشنهادهای آتش‌بس ایالات متحده که او روز قبل در نشست اسلو با ولودیمیر زلنسکی، رئیس جمهور اوکراین و دیگر متحدانش در میان گذاشته بود، مطلع کرد. در واقع، زلنسکی اعلام کرد که آتش‌بس را خواهد پذیرفت که خطوط فعلی را مسدود کند و به روسیه اجازه دهد به اشغال بخش‌های وسیعی از کشورش ادامه دهد. از سوی دیگر، پوتین پیش از این بارها از آمادگی برای گفتگو سخن گفته بود، اما پیش از هرگونه نشست واقعی، خواستار امتیازات یکجانبه شده بود. و نشست ویتکوف او بیشتر شبیه نمایشی از ادب بود که احتمالاً عمدتاً به خاطر لاف‌های خنده‌دار و چاپلوسانه ویتکوف در مورد «بشردوست» بودن پوتین به یاد خواهد ماند.
 در همین حال، دیگر مقامات روسی اعلام کردند که اوکراین باید «تصمیمات لازم» را اتخاذ کند یا شاهد «بدتر شدن» اوضاع خود باشد. این یک جبران بسیار ناچیز بود، پس از آنکه رئیس جمهور دونالد ترامپ ابتدا موافقت کرد که به مسکو اجازه دهد میلیون‌ها بشکه گازوئیل را به قیمت بازار بفروشد، تحریم‌های جاری را لغو کند و سپس تحریم‌های جدیدی را که به تازگی به قانون تبدیل کرده بود، لغو کند. کرملین یک گام مثبت کوچک برداشت و میزبان آمریکایی را آزاد کرد.

An Amazon employee claimed she was raped by a senior executive during a business trip to New York City — and that the company told her to keep quiet about it as it neglected to perform a full investigation of the allegations, according to an explosive lawsuit.

Laura Danbom, who works at Amazon’s Seattle headquarters as a marketing and operations manager for Amazon Web Services, sued the e-commerce giant this week for allegedly subjecting her to a hostile work environment and for violating Washington State’s Silenced No More Act, which protects victims who speak up about workplace assaults from retaliation.

The alleged rape took place on Oct. 27, 2023 when Danbom traveled to New York with a group of colleagues including Michelangelo Simonte, a top-performing advertising executive in her division who was based in Madrid, according to the complaint filed Tuesday.

That evening, the group attended an Amazon-hosted open bar event and continued the gathering at karaoke bars – all paid for by Amazon, according to the suit filed in state court in Seattle.

Early in the evening, Danbom and Simonte, who continues to work for Amazon at its Madrid offices, “flirted,” “joked” and “got along,” according to the complaint. At the end of the night, Simonte “kissed her,” and “persuaded Laura” to let him accompany her to her hotel room, the complaint said.

Danborn was staying at the Hyatt Place at 140 W. 24th St. in Manhattan’s trendy Chelsea neighborhood, according to a representative for the plaintiff. It was there that things took a wrong turn, the suit said.

“In Laura’s hotel room, during the early morning hours, Simonte raped her,” the complaint alleged. “Before the rape started, she said no. During the rape, Laura asked him: ‘you realize this is,’ and Simonte finished her sentence saying ‘rape? Yes.’ He ignored her protests. He raped her.”

The next day, she reported the incident to the New York Police Department, handing the officers a condom Simonte had left behind and submitting to a rape kit, according to the complaint.

During a phone call between Danbom and Simonte that a detective monitored for a potential confession, Simonte said he was “200% sure” that they never had sexual intercourse, according to the complaint.

Later, he contradicted himself in a police interview, saying he was too drunk to remember, according to the complaint.

Simonte did not immediately respond to a request for comment sent via LinkedIn.

The NYPD declined to refer the case to local prosecutors, said Danbom’s attorney Jay Free, adding that police said they had exhausted all investigative avenues. The complaint alleges that cops failed to interview the witnesses Danbom reported the rape to immediately after it occurred, including another Amazon employee. The Post has sought comment from the NYPD.

Two days after the alleged incident, Danbom informed Amazon’s human resources department. She also told a number of friends and her therapist about her experience, according the suit.

Amazon investigated the allegations, putting Simonte on a monthslong leave of absence, Danbom told The Post, but ultimately decided that he did not violate its policy.

Amazon claimed Danbom’s account of what happened was “unfounded due to lack of evidence,” and amounted to a “he said, she said” situation, according to the filing.

Danbom alleges that Amazon closed its investigation without speaking with witnesses who could corroborate her account and “without gathering evidence that was there for the asking,” according to the complaint.

It also claimed that during Amazon’s investigation, the company “asked inappropriate and re-traumatizing questions that suggested Laura did not do enough to stop the attack, including challenging Laura on whether she yelled ‘no,'” according to the complaint.

“Before the rape began, she said no. No means no,” the suit added. “This is shameful questioning by a leading employer in 2024.”

The company said it would reopen the case if New York prosecutors brought charges against Simonte, according to the suit. In addition, the company instructed Danbom “not to speak about Simonte’s rape at work saying the allegation was ‘highly confidential,’” according to the filing.

“It prevented me from warning other women who might interact with him at events,” Danbom told The Post.

Danbom was told that her role would not change at Amazon and that she would be required to “work with Simonte directly, by phone, by email and in remote meetings,” according to the filing.

“We take any allegation of this nature extremely seriously, and we have zero tolerance for workplace sexual misconduct or violence of any kind. We thoroughly investigate each report we receive and take appropriate action, up to and including termination, against those who are found to have violated our policies,” Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel said in a statement.

“We have robust policies and trained investigators in place to ensure each concern is heard and addressed with the proper care. While we don’t have more to share about the specifics of this pending litigation at this time, we continue to follow our rigorous processes and to hold all employees to the same high standards.”

Danbom told The Post she took two leaves of absence following the incident. After 10 job applications within Amazon, she was transferred in 2024 to a different position where she would not interact with Simonte, she said.

“It was really an escape,” she told The Post. “The position was a lateral move. I was on a path for a promotion and had to walk away from that.”

The complaint is seeking “lost wages, including front and backpay, lost bonuses and other benefits of employment, in an amount to be proven at trial.”
news.content: پوشش بیشتر ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود ببینید. بر اساس یک دادخواست جنجالی، یک کارمند آمازون ادعا کرد که در طول یک سفر کاری به شهر نیویورک توسط یک مدیر ارشد مورد تجاوز قرار گرفته است - و اینکه شرکت به او گفته است که در این مورد سکوت کند زیرا از انجام تحقیقات کامل در مورد این ادعاها غفلت کرده است. لورا دنبوم، که به عنوان مدیر بازاریابی و عملیات خدمات وب آمازون در دفتر مرکزی سیاتل آمازون کار می‌کند، این هفته از این غول تجارت الکترونیک به دلیل قرار دادن او در یک محیط کاری خصمانه و نقض قانون «دیگر سکوت ممنوع» ایالت واشنگتن شکایت کرد. این قانون از قربانیانی که در مورد حملات در محل کار صحبت می‌کنند در برابر انتقام‌جویی محافظت می‌کند. این تجاوز ادعایی در تاریخ 10 اکتبر رخ داده است. طبق شکایتی که روز سه‌شنبه ثبت شد، در ۲۷ دسامبر ۲۰۲۳، دانبوم به همراه گروهی از همکارانش از جمله میکل‌آنجلو سیمونته، مدیر اجرایی تبلیغات برتر در بخش خود که در مادرید مستقر بود، به نیویورک سفر کرد. عصر همان روز، این گروه در یک رویداد بار آزاد به میزبانی آمازون شرکت کردند و گردهمایی را در بارهای کارائوکه ادامه دادند - که طبق دادخواستی که در دادگاه ایالتی سیاتل ثبت شده، همه هزینه‌ها توسط آمازون پرداخت شده است. طبق این شکایت، اوایل شب، دنبوم و سیمونته، که همچنان در دفاتر مادرید آمازون کار می‌کند، «معاشقه»، «شوخی» و «با هم کنار آمدند». در پایان شب، سیمونته «او را بوسید» و «لورا را متقاعد کرد» که اجازه دهد او را تا اتاق هتلش همراهی کند. دنبورن در هتل هایت پلیس واقع در خیابان 140 غربی بیست و چهارم در چلسی شیک منهتن اقامت داشت.

New York’s social elite and Hollywood A-listers are conflicted over where they stand with Amy Griffin amid her ongoing scandals, a source exclusively told Page Six.

“People would like to distance themselves from her,” the insider told us, referring to her latest legal drama and alleged wedding outburst that has rattled members of her inner circle.

“People are outraged at the way she is behaving,” the source continued. “Everyone is talking about it. They are finding the whole thing to be distasteful.”

We hear that while several A-listers are eager to sever ties with Griffin, their business and financial entanglements with the venture capitalist have made them hesitant to do so.

Meanwhile, an insider shared with Page Six that other power players remain firmly on her side.

The G9 Ventures founder, notably, is a major investor in several celebrity companies, including Gwyneth Paltrow’s lifestyle brand, Goop, and Reese Witherspoon’s Hello Sunshine media company.

Griffin, 49, also holds stakes in Bumble and Spanx, and serves on both companies’ boards of directors.

Griffin has been navigating a legal dispute since March when a former classmate sued her, claiming the financier stole her account of childhood sexual abuse and portrayed it as her own story in her 2025 memoir, “The Tell.”

The businesswoman wrote in her book that she was raped by a teacher — and recovered memories of the alleged sexual assault during MDMA-assisted therapy.

In June, Griffin filed a defamation countersuit and denied adopting the other woman’s trauma.

While covering the scandal on his “Hot Mics” podcast in recent months, entertainment journalist Billy Bush has continued to cast doubt on the veracity of Griffin’s tell-all.

He claimed on Monday that he was accosted by Griffin at Jennifer Meyer’s star-studded wedding over his reporting.

Bush, 55, accused the “unhinged” writer of telling their fellow guests not to speak with him — with Demi Moore trying to convince her otherwise — before confronting him.

Bush insisted to podcast listeners he acted “calm and cool” during the interaction, telling Griffin, “OK, I can see you’re upset. I don’t think this is the time nor the place to have this discussion. I’d love to talk to you on the record and/or off. Either way, at another time, but not now.”

He claimed his girlfriend was also approached by Griffin at the Oct. 10 nuptials, with the writer asking, “How could you be with someone who’s abusing me?… He’s doing this for his entertainment.”

Bush dubbed Griffin a “narcissis[t]” with a lot of “nerve” and pointed out to his listeners, “This is another woman’s wedding. Imagine making it all about you?”

Reps for Griffin could not be reached for comment.

 ما شنیده‌ایم که در حالی که چندین چهره سرشناس مشتاق قطع همکاری با گریفین هستند، اما درگیری‌های تجاری و مالی آنها با این سرمایه‌گذار خطرپذیر، آنها را در انجام این کار مردد کرده است. در همین حال، یک منبع آگاه با پیج سیکس در میان گذاشت که سایر بازیگران قدرتمند همچنان قاطعانه از او حمایت می‌کنند. بنیانگذار G9 Ventures، به ویژه، سرمایه‌گذار اصلی چندین شرکت مشهور، از جمله برند سبک زندگی گوئینت پالترو، Goop، و شرکت رسانه‌ای Hello Sunshine ریس ویترسپون است. گریفین، ۴۹ ساله، همچنین در Bumble و Spanx سهام دارد و در هیئت مدیره هر دو شرکت فعالیت می‌کند. روز خود را با Page Six Daily آغاز کنید. لطفاً یک ایمیل معتبر وارد کنید. با کلیک روی بالا، شما با شرایط استفاده و سیاست حفظ حریم خصوصی موافقت می‌کنید. آیا می‌خواهید اخبار مربوط به سلبریتی‌ها را به محض انتشار آنها دنبال کنید؟ گریفین از ماه مارس درگیر یک دعوای حقوقی بوده است، زمانی که یکی از همکلاسی‌های سابقش از او شکایت کرد و ادعا کرد که این سرمایه‌دار، روایت او از سوءاستفاده جنسی در دوران کودکی را دزدیده و آن را به عنوان داستان خودش به تصویر کشیده است.

Shohei Ohtani avoided surgery after his injury-plagued 2026 season.

Dodgers backup catcher Dalton Rushing, however, wasn’t so lucky.

Rushing was set to undergo an internal brace procedure on Wednesday to address the damaged ligament in his right throwing elbow, according to multiple sources with knowledge of the situation.

The operation will come with a nine-month timeline to return to full catching duties, as the Los Angeles Times first reported, but the expectation is that he could be ready as a hitter by the beginning of next season.

Rushing initially hurt his elbow at the beginning of August, while playing catch in the outfield before the start of a game. He spent much of the final two months of the regular season on the injured list, returning for only six days in early September before going down again when he suffered a setback in his throwing progression.

Rushing was healthy enough to be activated for hitting-only duties during the final week of the regular season. However, he did not make the team’s postseason roster, bypassed by rookie sensation Josue De Paula as the team’s left-handed bench bat in October.

Now, more uncertainty awaits Rushing, who is two years removed from his debut as one of the club’s top prospects.

For all the strides he took in his second MLB campaign –– batting .246 with 12 home runs and 36 RBIs in 80 games, including an extended stint in June and July as the fill-in starter behind the plate during Will Smith’s neck injury –– his place in the team’s long-term plans remains unclear.

Rushing’s surgery likely opens a pathway for Hunter Feduccia to begin next season in the backup catcher role, where he impressed as Rushing’s replacement down the stretch this year.

Where Rushing will fit into the early-season roster is unknown.

Though he could still offer an option off the bench with his bat, there might be few opportunities for regular playing time with Shohei Ohtani entrenched as the designated hitter and Freddie Freeman at first base.

It’s all just another setback for the 25-year-old slugger, who has yet to truly flourish at the big-league level.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Cornell Green, a five-time Pro Bowl and Super Bowl-winning Cowboys defensive back, died Wednesday, the team announced.

No cause of death was provided.

Green spent his entire 13-year career (1962-74) in Dallas, where he was part of the famed “Doomsday Defense” that led the team to prominence. The two-time All-Pro First Team member appeared in two Super Bowls, winning one in 1972.

“We are sad to share news of the passing of Cowboys Legend Cornell Green this morning,” the Cowboys said in a statement. Cornell was a true trailblazer having never played football in college, yet becoming a multi-time Pro Bowler, All Pro and NFL Super Bowl Champion with the Cowboys playing defensive back from 1962 to 1974. He was a member of the 25th Anniversary Cowboys Team as well. Cornell remarkably never missed a game in 13 seasons, becoming one of the best and most dependable teammates to ever wear the star. Our thoughts and prayers are with his family.”

Green played just one season of high school football and did not play college football, but was invited to the Cowboys’ training camp in 1962, after which he was offered a spot on the team.

He accepted the offer despite being drafted by the NBA’s Chicago Zephyrs earlier that year after he was a two-time All-American basketball player for Utah State, later being enshrined in the school’s Hall of Fame.

In his 13 seasons, Green did not miss a game, starting 167 of 168 contests. He led the Cowboys in interceptions four times and finished with 34 career interceptions, which ties him for fifth in team history.

Green played in two NFL Championship Games and Super Bowls V and VI, with the Cowboys defeating the Dolphins 24-3 in the latter.

Green retired after the 1974 season and later became a scout for the Cowboys and Broncos, earning AFC Scout of the Year honors in 2010.

For his efforts as a player, he was named to the Cowboys 25th Anniversary Team in 1984.

پوشش بیشتر ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود ببینید. تیم کابوی‌ها اعلام کرد که کرنل گرین، مدافع خط حمله‌ای که پنج بار قهرمان پرو بول و سوپر بول شده بود، روز چهارشنبه درگذشت. هیچ علت مرگی اعلام نشده است. گرین تمام دوران حرفه‌ای ۱۳ ساله خود (۱۹۶۲-۱۹۷۴) را در دالاس گذراند، جایی که بخشی از تیم معروف «دفاع روز رستاخیز» بود که تیم را به اوج رساند. این بازیکن که دو بار عضو تیم اول آل پرو شده بود، در دو سوپر بول حضور داشت و یکی را در سال ۱۹۷۲ برنده شد. کابوی‌ها در بیانیه‌ای اعلام کردند: «ما از اعلام خبر درگذشت اسطوره کابوی‌ها، کورنل گرین، امروز صبح بسیار متاسفیم.» کورنل یک پیشگام واقعی بود که هرگز در دانشگاه فوتبال بازی نکرده بود، اما با این حال چندین بار به عنوان بولر حرفه‌ای، قهرمان تمام حرفه‌ای‌ها و قهرمان سوپربول NFL با کابوی‌ها از سال ۱۹۶۲ تا ۱۹۷۴ بازی کرد. او همچنین عضو تیم کابوی‌ها در بیست و پنجمین سالگرد تأسیسشان بود. کرنل به طرز چشمگیری در ۱۳ فصل حتی یک بازی را هم از دست نداد و به یکی از بهترین و قابل اعتمادترین هم‌تیمی‌هایی تبدیل شد که تا به حال این ستاره را پوشیده‌اند. با خانواده‌اش ابراز همدردی و دعا می‌کنیم.
 گرین فقط یک فصل در دبیرستان فوتبال بازی کرد و در دانشگاه فوتبال بازی نکرد، اما در سال ۱۹۶۲ به اردوی تمرینی کابوی‌ها دعوت شد و پس از آن به او پیشنهاد حضور در تیم داده شد. او با وجود اینکه اوایل همان سال توسط تیم شیکاگو زفیرز از NBA درفت شده بود، این پیشنهاد را پذیرفت. او دو بار بازیکن منتخب آمریکا برای تیم دانشگاه ایالتی یوتا بود و بعدها نامش در تالار مشاهیر این دانشگاه ثبت شد. گرین در ۱۳ فصل حضورش در این تیم، حتی یک بازی را هم از دست نداد و در ۱۶۷ مسابقه از ۱۶۸ مسابقه، در ترکیب اصلی قرار گرفت. او رهبری تیم کاب را بر عهده داشت.

The push by Lindsay Clancy’s lawyer to investigate the lone holdout juror who forced a mistrial in her triple-murder case has been stopped in its tracks by the judge.

Clancy’s defense attorney, Kevin Reddington, had asked for an evidentiary hearing at an upcoming Nov. 2 court date to call witnesses to speak about accusations that Michael P. Desronvil lied on his jury questionnaire and used his cellphone during deliberations.

However, Judge William F. Sullivan wasn’t having it, and ruled Wednesday that the mistrial must only be evaluated based on the circumstances known at the time.

Additionally, Sullivan ruled that inquiring further into the juror’s reasoning or the jury’s internal deliberations would be inappropriate.

While Clancy’s motion to dismiss the charges remains pending, both sides are scheduled to present their arguments on Nov. 2.

news.originalContent:
Manchester United winless run continues with 4-1 Champions League humbling in Como, and Bruno Fernandes slams tactics.

Manchester United captain Bruno ‌Fernandes said his side failed to apply enough pressure and adopted ⁠a “mood of defeat” ⁠after conceding early in Wednesday’s 4–1 Champions League loss at Como, a result that increased scrutiny on manager Michael Carrick.

Como opened the scoring ⁠in the second minute, and United collapsed, with only a stoppage-time consolation goal from Joshua Zirkzee making the scoreline slightly less severe.

“We started on the wrong ⁠foot, and they scored very early,” Fernandes told TNT Sports. “There was not enough pressure on the ball and not many good movements off the ball. There were many things not going our way.

“It’s a decision from the [coaching] staff not to press man-to-man ‌and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said.

Asked if his comments amounted to criticism of Carrick’s tactics, Fernandes said: “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me.

“Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and ⁠making them uncomfortable.”

Carrick has come under increasing pressure with ⁠United now winless in seven matches.

“It was more than disappointing,” the 45-year-old manager told TNT Sports. “I think everybody’s got to take responsibility for that. I’ll take responsibility for the overall team and performance; it stops with me, and I’m fine with that.

“But as a supporter of this football club, to see a ⁠performance like that is unacceptable, I have to ⁠say.”

Carrick said his side had failed to show the required intensity.

“It’s the motivation and the purpose and the intensity of a game of football that you have to bring. We didn’t bring that today,” ‌he said. “I’ve got to apologise for the performance.”

Fernandes also questioned United’s mentality after the early setback.

“Conceding early makes us go into the game with a mood ‌of ‌defeat,” he said.

United have three points from their opening three Champions League matches and host AS Roma in their next fixture in the competition.
news.content:
روند بدون برد منچستریونایتد با شکست تحقیرآمیز ۴-۱ در کومو در لیگ قهرمانان اروپا ادامه دارد و برونو فرناندز تاکتیک‌ها را مورد انتقاد قرار می‌دهد. برونو فرناندز، کاپیتان منچستریونایتد، گفت که تیمش پس از دریافت گل زودهنگام در شکست ۴-۱ چهارشنبه شب لیگ قهرمانان اروپا در کومو، به اندازه کافی فشار نیاورد و «حالت شکست» به خود گرفت. این نتیجه باعث افزایش بررسی‌ها روی سرمربی تیم، مایکل کریک، شد. کومو در دقیقه دوم گل اول را زد و یونایتد از هم پاشید، تنها یک گل تسلی‌بخش در وقت‌های اضافه از جاشوا زیرکزی، اوضاع را کمی آرام‌تر کرد. فرناندز به TNT Sports گفت: «ما بازی را با پای اشتباه شروع کردیم و آنها خیلی زود به گل رسیدند. فشار کافی روی توپ وجود نداشت و حرکات خوبی هم بدون توپ انجام نمی‌شد. خیلی چیزها مطابق میل ما پیش نمی‌رفت. او گفت: «این تصمیم کادر مربیگری است که حریف را نفر به نفر پرس نکنند و گاهی اوقات فضا را پشت سر بگذارند و سعی کنند توپ را بگیرند، منتظر آنها بمانند، اما گاهی اوقات وقتی به این تیم‌ها فضا می‌دهید، اعتماد به نفس پیدا می‌کنند.» فرناندز در پاسخ به این سوال که آیا اظهاراتش به معنای انتقاد از تاکتیک‌های کریک است، گفت: «این را باید سرمربی و کادر فنی ببینند، نه من.» «بعضی وقت‌ها باید زیر فشار شجاع‌تر باشی، ریسک فشار آوردن به حریف و ⁠ایجاد ناراحتی برای آنها را بپذیری.»
 کریک با توجه به اینکه یونایتد اکنون در هفت بازی بدون برد بوده، تحت فشار فزاینده‌ای قرار گرفته است. این مربی ۴۵ ساله به TNT Sports گفت: «این چیزی فراتر از ناامیدکننده بود. فکر می‌کنم همه باید مسئولیت آن را بپذیرند. من مسئولیت کلی را بر عهده می‌گیرم.»

news.originalContent:
Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande score stunners as Real beat Leipzig to make it three from three in Champions League.

Real Madrid claimed a third Champions League victory in as many games, thrashing RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday, with Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande among the goalscorers for Jose Mourinho’s side.

Bernardo Silva opened the scoring for Madrid from close range late in a tight first half, with Arda Guler doubling the advantage of the record 15-time European champions soon after the interval.

Mbappe bent home a third before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back for the German side, and Diomande rammed a volley into the top corner late on to cap Madrid’s triumph.

Their fourth consecutive win across all competitions will boost Madrid’s morale ahead of Sunday’s La Liga Clasico against bitter rivals Barcelona.

Without a major trophy in two seasons and after a shaky domestic start, Madrid can at least boast a perfect record in Europe, unlike Barca after their defeat at Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday.

Mourinho started Vinicius, serving a four-match ban in La Liga, on the left flank and benched former Leipzig winger Diomande, despite his improving form.

The coach also brought Bernardo Silva and Eduardo Camavinga into midfield and put midfielder Federico Valverde at right-back again, as he did in Sunday’s win at Sevilla.

Visitors Leipzig created the first big chance, with Madrid stopper Thibaut Courtois getting down low to make a superb save from Romulo Cardoso.

Vinicius, who improved on a poor showing at Roma last week without breaking out of his rut, drew a full-stretch save from Leipzig’s Maarten Vandevoordt.

Madrid carved out an advantage in the final stages of a low-key first half when Valverde cut the ball back for Guler, whose shot Vandevoordt saved. However, the goalkeeper could not clear it, and Silva darted in to prod over the line.

It was the former Manchester City midfielder’s first goal for the club after joining this summer.

Vandevoordt saved well from Valverde’s fierce effort before Guler put Madrid two goals ahead in the 52nd minute.

Jude Bellingham crossed to the back post and Mbappe nodded the ball across goal, with Guler able to hold off a defender and turn home.

Mbappe lashed a shot into the side netting after Bellingham teed it up, as Madrid looked to put the game out of sight.

Mourinho sent on Diomande for Vinicius with 20 minutes remaining, and the Brazilian looked disappointed on the bench, knowing he cannot play again until November 4, when Madrid visit AEK Athens.

Madrid’s record 140 million-euro ($157m) signing, Diomande, pulled the ball back to Mbappe on the edge of the box for Madrid’s third, and the French forward bent it home.

Leipzig quickly grabbed a consolation goal at the other end as Dean Huijsen switched off, with Gomis firing past Courtois.

Diomande ended proceedings with a bang, rattling an emphatic volley from Brahim Diaz’s cross into the top corner for his third goal in his last four appearances.

news.originalContent:
Eze gave Arsenal the lead, but Davies levelled and Kane netted a penalty for the hosts before Rice made it 2-2.

Declan Rice scored a late equaliser to grab last season’s runners-up Arsenal a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich in the Champions League.

Eberechi Eze opened the scoring for Arsenal on Wednesday after coming on for the injured Bukayo Saka, but Alphonso Davies brought Bayern level after a sublime pass from Harry Kane.

Kane had Bayern on track for victory when he created and converted a second-half penalty, but his England teammate Rice equalised with eight minutes remaining to earn Arsenal a point.

Bayern were without in-form winger Michael Olise, Germany captain Joshua Kimmich and midfielder Jamal Musiala. Coach Vincent Kompany had been a doubt due to illness but took his place in the dugout.

Despite the absences, Kane ensured Bayern posed a consistent threat against Arsenal’s miserly defence with another excellent performance ahead of next week’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in London.

Kane’s second-half penalty, his 16th goal in 23 matches against Arsenal, extended his scoring streak to 10 straight Champions League games. Kane is one shy of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo, who scored in 11 consecutive matches for Real Madrid.

The draw was just the second time Arsenal had dropped points in 12 games in all competitions this season.

Arsenal were hit with an early blow when Saka, their joint-top scorer this season, fell to the ground eight minutes in, grabbed his thigh and immediately signalled to the bench.

Bayern’s two previous Champions League opponents this term were from Norway, and the perennial Bundesliga winners seemed to struggle with Arsenal’s physicality as Mikel Arteta’s side pinned them back in the early stages.

With 25 minutes gone, Odegaard floated a simple pass across Bayern’s defence and into the path of the onrushing Eze, who collected and stroked the ball past Manuel Neuer.

Caught out by Eze’s perfectly timed run, the hosts looked even more surprised when VAR overturned the linesman’s offside call and awarded the goal.

The pre-match chatter had been dominated by talk of Kane’s Ballon d’Or prospects, and the England captain showed why he is among the favourites when he set up Davies’s equaliser 10 minutes later.

Kane spotted Davies on the move and threaded the ball through the midfield and around Gabriel for the Canadian winger to guide the ball into the bottom corner.

With the hosts now in the ascendancy, Ezri Konsa saw yellow for taking Kane out of a Bayern counter minutes later.

After the break, Neuer and David Raya took turns producing magnificent saves, with the Bayern captain tipping Bruno Guimaraes’s header onto the crossbar and the Spaniard denying Dayot Upamecano.

Both sides traded surges forward, but Kane would again prove crucial as Bayern took the lead.

Kane’s shot from the edge of the penalty area connected with Jurrien Timber’s arm, with the referee immediately pointing to the spot before Kane stepped up and buried his kick.

Bayern looked to be in control but the match turned again when late substitute Viktor Gyokeres threaded a clever pass to Rice, who slammed in an equaliser.

Kane told TNT Sports he was a little disappointed with the result.

“But probably when you look at the whole 90 minutes, a draw was probably a fair result,” he said.

news.originalContent:
The alleged participation of US agents in an April drug operation has raised questions about whether Mexican law was upheld.

Mexico has taken the rare step of charging a former state prosecutor with treason, alleging that he allowed United States agents to take part in a drug raid on the country’s territory.

The case underscores sensitivities about US involvement in Mexico and concerns about the Latin American country’s sovereignty.

On Wednesday, former Chihuahua Attorney General Cesar Jauregui was accused of permitting US agents to take part in an antidrug operation in the northwestern border state.

Under Mexican law, the federal government must approve the activities of foreign forces on the country’s soil.

But questions emerged about whether the law was being adhered to after two US agents and two Mexican law enforcement officials were killed in a car accident on April 19.

News outlets, citing anonymous sources, reported that the US agents had been collaborating with state law enforcement in the destruction of a drug lab.

Matias Gomez Leautaud, an analyst at the Eurasia Group, a US-based risk consultancy firm, told the news service Reuters that the treason charge “seeks to set a precedent and prevent cooperation between [Mexican] states and the US government without the federal government’s coordination and approval”.

While the administration of President Claudia Sheinbaum has collaborated with the US on issues of crime and insecurity, it has opposed any effort by the US to work directly with Mexican states without federal authorisation first.

In the days after the April car crash, Sheinbaum indicated that her government was not aware that US agents had been involved in a drug operation in Chihuahua.

“Evidently, the military didn’t know there were people participating who weren’t Mexican citizens,” Sheinbaum told reporters at the time.

She called for an investigation into whether state officials had respected Mexico’s constitution and its National Security Law, which govern the involvement of foreign forces on Mexican territory.

The constitution, for example, requires Senate approval for the presence of any foreign troops in Mexico. The country has a long history of US intervention, including multiple military invasions continuing into the early 20th century.

But concerns about the US respecting Mexican sovereignty have risen since US President Donald Trump returned to office for a second term.

Trump has suggested that the US could take unilateral military action in Mexico to address cartel drug-trafficking and violence, and he has characterised Mexico’s government as ineffective in addressing the problem.

“We have to eradicate them,” Trump said of the cartels in March. “We have to knock the hell out of them because they’re getting worse. They’re taking over their country. The cartels are running Mexico.”

In the aftermath of the April crash, conflicting reports emerged about why the two US agents were in the country.

Media identified them as members of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), a US foreign intelligence branch with a history of covert operations.

But state officials denied claims that they were involved in a drug bust. In a news release on April 20, Jauregui “ruled out the involvement of foreign personnel” in his state’s drug operations.

Instead, he said that US instructors had been present nearby for a training session about drones. They subsequently requested to join a convoy of Mexican law enforcement personnel to return to the airport, according to Jauregui.

“It is worth explaining what happened, in order to clarify the facts that are causing some confusion,” Jauregui said at the time.

He resigned from his post as state attorney general later that month.

Mexico has taken the rare step of charging a former state prosecutor with treason, alleging that he allowed United States agents to take part in a drug raid on the country’s territory.

The case underscores sensitivities about US involvement in Mexico and concerns about the Latin American country’s sovereignty.

On Wednesday, former Chihuahua Attorney General Cesar Jauregui was accused of permitting US agents to take part in an antidrug operation in the northwestern border state.

Under Mexican law, the federal government must approve the activities of foreign forces on the country’s soil.

But questions emerged about whether the law was being adhered to after two US agents and two Mexican law enforcement officials were killed in a car accident on April 19.

News outlets, citing anonymous sources, reported that the US agents had been collaborating with state law enforcement in the destruction of a drug lab.

Matias Gomez Leautaud, an analyst at the Eurasia Group, a US-based risk consultancy firm, told the news service Reuters that the treason charge “seeks to set a precedent and prevent cooperation between [Mexican] states and the US government without the federal government’s coordination and approval”.

While the administration of President Claudia Sheinbaum has collaborated with the US on issues of crime and insecurity, it has opposed any effort by the US to work directly with Mexican states without federal authorisation first.

In the days after the April car crash, Sheinbaum indicated that her government was not aware that US agents had been involved in a drug operation in Chihuahua.

“Evidently, the military didn’t know there were people participating who weren’t Mexican citizens,” Sheinbaum told reporters at the time.

She called for an investigation into whether state officials had respected Mexico’s constitution and its National Security Law, which govern the involvement of foreign forces on Mexican territory.

The constitution, for example, requires Senate approval for the presence of any foreign troops in Mexico. The country has a long history of US intervention, including multiple military invasions continuing into the early 20th century.

Trump has suggested that the US could take unilateral military action in Mexico to address cartel drug-trafficking and violence, and he has characterised Mexico’s government as ineffective in addressing the problem.

news.originalContent:
Race between sibling of former Senator Lindsey Graham, Democrat Annie Andrews has tightened in deep-red state.

United States President Donald Trump is set to travel to South Carolina to boost the campaign of Darline Graham, the sister of his close ally, the late Senator Lindsey Graham.

The visit on Wednesday, which will include a rally alongside Graham, comes as the Senate race in deep-red South Carolina has grown uncomfortably close for Republicans.

Lindsey Graham, long one of the most hawkish members of the Senate who was an outspoken supporter of the US-Israel war on Iran, had been expected to sail to victory in the November 3 vote. But his unexpected death in July upended the race.

South Carolina’s governor tapped Darline Graham to finish her brother’s term. Trump then made the surprise move of endorsing Graham in a new Republican primary, helping her to claim the party’s nomination. The president said the endorsement was “in honour of her brother”.

In a video message last week, Trump again said Graham had his unconditional support.

“I’m asking everyone in South Carolina to get out and vote for a wonderful person, a great woman … a woman that Lindsey Graham said is the greatest person he’s ever met,” Trump said.

Democratic challenger Annie Andrews, a medical doctor and paediatrician, has seized on Graham’s inexperience and her unorthodox route to the Republican nomination.

Speaking to a local Fox News affiliate before Trump’s rally in Pendleton, South Carolina, Andrews pointed to Graham’s lacklustre debate performance, including one instance where she said she was “not that informed on national security”.

“My opponent needs the highest level of federal government politicians to speak for her. On the debate stage, it was really clear,” Andrews said.

Graham, meanwhile, has called Andrews “the most radical liberal that’s ever run for state office in South Carolina”.

Polls have shown Graham leading by about 2.7 percentage points, according to a Real Clear Politics average. Trump carried the state by 18 percentage points in 2024.

Trump’s visit comes after the president issued an executive order waiving most sanctions and tariffs on Russia, established by a law named after Lindsey Graham and passed with bipartisan support in 2026.

The move prompted a tempered rebuke from Darline Graham.

“Personally, I would choose to put the ⁠pressure on Russia to end the war and get gas prices down,” she told The Associated Press news agency on Saturday.

“I don’t trust Putin, and I don’t trust Russia,” she said.

The executive order on sanctions has been part of a wider Trump administration shift in its approach to ending the war with Ukraine, which began with Russia’s invasion in February 2024.

Trump and his allies have heaped pressure on Ukraine, framing its leader, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, as the main impediment to peace. In turn, Washington has offered several concessions to Russia, including a deal to buy Russian diesel.

Lindsey Graham had been a staunch supporter of Ukraine. His death came shortly after he returned from his 10th visit to the country since the war began.

The tightening race in South Carolina underscores the harsh political reality for Republicans heading into the final stretch of the midterms.

Trump has sought to use his political clout to bring party loyalists out to vote, campaigning in strongholds across the country. But the president heads into the vote with the lowest approval ratings of his career, with voters expressing dismay about affordability and the knock-on effects of the US-Israel war with Iran.

Beyond South Carolina, other one-time Republican strongholds have shown signs of shifting towards Democrats.

That includes Kansas, where polls suggest Republican Ashley Hinson is effectively tied with Democrat Joshua Turek. The state, where farmers have been particularly hard hit by rising prices on fuel and equipment, has not sent a Democrat to the Senate since 1939.

Trump also broke from the Republican establishment to endorse Attorney General Ken Paxton over Senator John Cornyn in the Texas primary. Polling averages show Paxton, whose career has been marred by a procession of scandals, trailing behind Democratic challenger Talarico by 1.7 percentage points. The race is widely considered a toss-up.

A Republican has not won statewide office in Texas since 1994.

news.originalContent:
A jury found Meta guilty of lying to Facebook users in ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠New Mexico about access to their data.

A United States judge has ordered Meta to pay $25bn after a jury found the company misled Facebook users about privacy violations, marking the biggest fine ever against the tech giant.

New Mexico state District Judge Francis Mathew issued the ruling on Wednesday.

“Facebook promised users that they (the users) controlled their data. This was false,” he said.

Last month, a jury found Meta responsible for more than 43 million violations of New Mexico’s consumer protection laws. New Mexico Attorney General Raul Torrez highlighted that the decision was one of the largest state verdicts against a company in US history.

“This judgement should be a signal, an unambiguous message, to Silicon Valley,” Torrez said at a news conference.

Meta lawyer Matt Nicholson argued in court that a sum as high as $40bn would be “shocking to the conscience”, while a lawyer for New Mexico, Randi McGinn, urged standing up to “tech titans who think they are bulletproof and can do whatever they want”.

“The jury didn’t make findings that any New Mexican heard or saw these statements, or was harmed by them,” Nicholson argued during a hearing held early this month.

Torrez told reporters following the verdict that all the money awarded would go into a fund for the state’s education system.

The amount awarded in the case far exceeds the $5bn fine that the Federal Trade Commission levied against Facebook in 2019.

New Mexico accused Meta of misleading users about who could access their personal information and how harmful content was handled on its platforms. Jurors found that 26 of 29 statements made by Meta and its leadership on privacy and content moderation were misleading.

Meta plans to appeal the verdict, potentially reducing the final payment amount.

In a statement, CJ Mahoney, Meta’s chief legal officer, said the company is confident it will win on appeal.

“This ruling, and the Attorney General’s approach to this enforcement, makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico,” Mahoney said. “At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online.”

The lawsuit, filed in 2021, stemmed partly from revelations that Cambridge Analytica, a British political consulting firm that is now defunct, had obtained personal data from as many as 87 million Facebook users without their consent and used it to develop targeted political advertisements. Its clients included President Donald Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign.

The case, a major setback for the tech giant, marks the second legal defeat for Meta in New Mexico in six months. In March, a jury found the company misled users about the safety of young people on Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, ordering it to pay $375m in civil penalties. Meta was later ordered to make an additional $567m payment into a state fund for teen mental health and was required to implement measures to protect young users.

زهره حنکیر، خبرنگار، به بخش زنان جهان بی‌بی‌سی می‌گوید: «وقتی فرسنگ‌ها دورتر از وطن در آپارتمانم در بروکلین خط چشم می‌کشم احساس می‌کنم با مادرم و مادر‌بزرگم و همه زنان خاور‌میانه پیوند برقرار می‌کنم».

یونسکو، آژانس فرهنگی سازمان ملل متحد با تعیین سرمه به عنوان میراث فرهنگی ناملموس بشری، اهمیت سرمه یا کحل عربی را به رسمیت شناخته است.

سرمه، ماده‌ای تیره‌رنگ که از دیرباز زنان و مردان آن را به دور چشم‌های خود می‌کشیده‌اند، پیشینه‌ای دارد که به هزاران سال پیش و تمدن‌های باستانی می‌رسد.

در جهان عرب آن را «کحل» می‌نامند، اما در نقاط دیگر با نام‌های متفاوتی شناخته می‌شود؛ «کاجال» در جنوب آسیا، «تیرو» در نیجریه و «سرمه» در ایران. سرمه به طور سنتی از آنتیموان، سرب یا دیگر مواد معدنی ساخته می‌شد، اما در محصولات امروزیِ سرمه از ترکیبات دیگری نیز استفاده می‌شود.

این ماده آرایشی جایگاه ویژه‌ای برای خانم حنکیر نویسنده لبنانی‌ـ‌بریتانیایی دارد که خانواده‌اش در هنگامه جنگ داخلی ۱۹۷۵ در لبنان به انگلستان نقل مکان کرده‌اند.

او توضیح می‌دهد: «وقتی دور از وطن زندگی می‌کردیم، مادرم را تماشا می‌کردم که آرایش می‌کرد. احساس می‌کردم او از این طریق با چیزی بسیار عمیق پیوند برقرار می‌کند.»

او می‌گوید همان پیوندی را که در آن لحظه در مادرش می‌دید، هنگام کشیدن خط چشم خود نیز احساس می‌کند.

خانم حنکیر، نویسنده کتاب تاریخچه فرهنگی خط‌چشم می‌گوید به رسمیت شناختن سرمه به عنوان میراث فرهنگی ناملموس «نه تکیه بر مارک و محصول خاص بلکه تاکید بر این رفتار فرهنگی دارد که شایسته مراقبت و ماندگاری است».

او توضیح می‌دهد: «به رسمیت‌شناسی کمک می‌کند که چنین دانش و آداب و رسوم و همچنین هنر و پیشه مربوط به تهیه سرمه و استفاده از سرمه حفظ شود و باقی بماند و اطمینان از اینکه همه اینها مستند و ثبت شوند و به نسل‌های بعدی منتقل شوند، نه اینکه در میان فرهنگ زیبایی تجاری جهانی کمرنگ شوند و از یاد بروند».

جرقه این کنجکاوی زمانی زده شد که او در یکی از مهمانی‌های شام، قوطی سرمه‌ای را که همراه داشت به دوست ایرانی‌اش نشان داد. گفت‌وگو درباره تاریخچه و بار نمادین سرمه، هنکیر را بر آن داشت تا درباره گذشته این ماده و تاریخ استفاده از خط چشم تحقیق کند.

او می‌گوید: «برای من مهم این بود که دریافتم سرمه برای زنان، به‌ویژه زنان اقلیت و زنانی که در مهاجرت و دور از زادگاه خود زندگی می‌کنند، معنایی بسیار فراتر از آرایش دارد.»

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

ریشه سرمه به تمدن‌های باستان در مصر، میان‌رودان یا بین‌النهرین و ایران باز‌می‌گردد. به گفته خانم حنکیر در مصر باستان همه افراد فارغ از جنسیت و طبقه اجتماعی از سرمه استفاده می‌کردند.

او می‌گوید: «آنها از سرمه به دلایلی فراتر از زیبایی استفاده می‌کردند» و توضیح می‌دهد سرمه کشیدن نوعی احساس معنویت برای آنها ایجاد می‌کرد و از چشمان آنها در برابر بیماری‌ها محافظت می‌کرد.

«مصریان باستان سرمه‌دان افراد را با مردگان دفن می‌کردند تا با خود به زندگی پس از مرگ ببرند و این نشان از اهمیت سرمه برای آنها داشت».

خانم حنکیر می‌گوید ملکه مصر نفرتی‌تی در مورد استفاده از سرمه «اینفلوئنسر» واقعی زمان خودش بوده است.

سردیس مشهور نفر‌تی‌تی که گروه باستان‌شناس آلمانی به سرپرستی لودوویگ بورچارت در سال۱۹۱۲ در مصر کشف کردند نشان از کاربرد دقیق خط چشم با سرمه دارد.

زهره حنکیر در کتاب خود می‌نویسد: «او ابرو‌های کمانی خوش‌نقش و بی‌نظیری داشته است که با رنگ سیاه مایل به خاکستری که می‌تواند سرمه باشد رنگ شده‌اند. تضاد رنگ شدید است اما چهره و ظاهر ملکه بی‌نقص به نظر می‌رسد».

هنکیر می‌گوید زنان در آلمان برای شبیه شدن به ظاهر «شرقی» و متفاوت او، از سرمه استفاده می‌کردند و آن را با زیبایی، اقتدار و توانمندی پیوند می‌دادند.

شیوه آرایش ملکه باستانی مصر نفر‌تی‌تی هنوز مد روز است.

زهره حنکیر در کتابش می‌نویسد: «صد‌ها روش آموزش در یوتیوب، تیک‌تاک و اینستاگرام برای شیوه آرایش ملکه با دقت و ریز‌بینی فراوان رواج دارد».

پژوهش خانم حنکیر درباره خط چشم و سرمه او را به گرداگرد جهان کشانده است. از کرالا (ایالتی در هند) تا چاد، مکزیک، اردن و ژاپن و او در سفرهایش دریافته است که هرچند خط چشم به طور گسترده در جهان به شکل‌ها و معانی و شیوه‌های مختلف رواج دارد اما نقش آن به عنوان شیوه‌ای برای محافظت چشم یکی از دلایل اصلی کاربرد آن است.

خط چشم در موارد گوناگونی از محافظت چشم در برابر آفتاب تا استفاده در آداب و رسوم مذهبی برای دفع «چشم‌زخم» و همچنین برای اهداف درمانی استفاده می‌شود.

او در ژاپن با گیشاها، هنرمندان سنتی ژاپنی که در موسیقی، رقص و هنر گفت‌وگو مهارت دارند، دیدار کرد. آنها از خط چشم قرمز استفاده می‌کردند؛ نمادی برای محافظت در برابر نیروهای شر که هنوز هم رواج دارد.

او می‌گوید در فرهنگ «چولا» میان آمریکایی‌های مکزیکی‌تبار، خط چشم نمادی قدرتمند از هویت، مقاومت و غرور فرهنگی به شمار می‌رود.

خانم حنکیر مشاهده کرده است که درست مانند مصر باستان در بخش‌هایی از جهان فقط زنان نیستند که از خط چشم استفاده می‌کنند.

در چاد خانم حنکیر مدتی را با وادابی، گروه کوچ‌نشین فولانی گذراند که به دلیل مسابقات زیبایی سالانه که زنان زیبایی مردان را داوری می‌کنند مشهور است.

زهره حنکیر با خنده می‌گوید: «مردان بادیه‌نشین در پترا واقع در اردن از خط چشم نه فقط برای محافظت در برابر آفتاب یا نمادی دینی استفاده می‌کنند بلکه خوب می‌دانند که خط چشم آنها را زیباتر می‌کند».

«خط چشم برای آنها نوعی نشانه مردانگی و همچنین علامتی برای مجرد بودن است».

خط چشم با سرمه اغلب برای چشمان کودکان هم استفاده می‌شود که برخی معتقدند خاصیت حفاظتی دارد.

در کشورهای عربی‌زبان نام‌هایی مانند «کحل» و «کحیلان» و در ایران نیز نام «سرمه» رواج دارد؛ نام‌هایی که بازتاب‌دهنده اهمیت فرهنگی سرمه و خط چشم هستند.

خانم هنکیر می‌گوید ثبت سرمه در فهرست میراث فرهنگی ناملموس یونسکو «بسیار دیرهنگام» بود و در عین حال «ادای دینی است به جوامع جنوب جهانی، به‌ویژه در سراسر جهان عرب، که این سنت را در طول قرن‌ها حفظ کرده و زنده نگه داشته‌اند؛ آن هم اغلب در برابر آوارگی، استعمار و تلاش برای زدودن هویت فرهنگی.»

برای این نویسنده پیوند سرمه با فرهنگ ملی خودش باعث شده است که استفاده از آن برایش اهمیت فراوانی پیدا کند.

او می‌گوید: «برای من سرمه کشیدن کاری معنوی است. وقتی سرمه به چشمانم می‌کشم انگار کاری آئینی انجام می‌دهم. این کار معنای فراتر از کشیدن یک خط زیر چشم یا بالای چشم دارد».

زهره حنکیر، خبرنگار، به بخش زنان جهان بی‌بی‌سی می‌گوید: «وقتی فرسنگ‌ها دورتر از وطن در آپارتمانم در بروکلین خط چشم می‌کشم احساس می‌کنم با مادرم و مادر‌بزرگم و همه زنان خاور‌میانه پیوند برقرار می‌کنم».

یونسکو، آژانس فرهنگی سازمان ملل متحد با تعیین سرمه به عنوان میراث فرهنگی ناملموس بشری، اهمیت سرمه یا کحل عربی را به رسمیت شناخته است.

سرمه، ماده‌ای تیره‌رنگ که از دیرباز زنان و مردان آن را به دور چشم‌های خود می‌کشیده‌اند، پیشینه‌ای دارد که به هزاران سال پیش و تمدن‌های باستانی می‌رسد.

در جهان عرب آن را «کحل» می‌نامند، اما در نقاط دیگر با نام‌های متفاوتی شناخته می‌شود؛ «کاجال» در جنوب آسیا، «تیرو» در نیجریه و «سرمه» در ایران. سرمه به طور سنتی از آنتیموان، سرب یا دیگر مواد معدنی ساخته می‌شد، اما در محصولات امروزیِ سرمه از ترکیبات دیگری نیز استفاده می‌شود.

این ماده آرایشی جایگاه ویژه‌ای برای خانم حنکیر نویسنده لبنانی‌ـ‌بریتانیایی دارد که خانواده‌اش در هنگامه جنگ داخلی ۱۹۷۵ در لبنان به انگلستان نقل مکان کرده‌اند.

او توضیح می‌دهد: «وقتی دور از وطن زندگی می‌کردیم، مادرم را تماشا می‌کردم که آرایش می‌کرد. احساس می‌کردم او از این طریق با چیزی بسیار عمیق پیوند برقرار می‌کند.»

او می‌گوید همان پیوندی را که در آن لحظه در مادرش می‌دید، هنگام کشیدن خط چشم خود نیز احساس می‌کند.

خانم حنکیر، نویسنده کتاب تاریخچه فرهنگی خط‌چشم می‌گوید به رسمیت شناختن سرمه به عنوان میراث فرهنگی ناملموس «نه تکیه بر مارک و محصول خاص بلکه تاکید بر این رفتار فرهنگی دارد که شایسته مراقبت و ماندگاری است».

او توضیح می‌دهد: «به رسمیت‌شناسی کمک می‌کند که چنین دانش و آداب و رسوم و همچنین هنر و پیشه مربوط به تهیه سرمه و استفاده از سرمه حفظ شود و باقی بماند و اطمینان از اینکه همه اینها مستند و ثبت شوند و به نسل‌های بعدی منتقل شوند، نه اینکه در میان فرهنگ زیبایی تجاری جهانی کمرنگ شوند و از یاد بروند».

جرقه این کنجکاوی زمانی زده شد که او در یکی از مهمانی‌های شام، قوطی سرمه‌ای را که همراه داشت به دوست ایرانی‌اش نشان داد. گفت‌وگو درباره تاریخچه و بار نمادین سرمه، هنکیر را بر آن داشت تا درباره گذشته این ماده و تاریخ استفاده از خط چشم تحقیق کند.

او می‌گوید: «برای من مهم این بود که دریافتم سرمه برای زنان، به‌ویژه زنان اقلیت و زنانی که در مهاجرت و دور از زادگاه خود زندگی می‌کنند، معنایی بسیار فراتر از آرایش دارد.»

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

news.originalContent:
Tammy Cramer remembers when her grandchildren spent their summers pushing each other into Cedar Lake from the inflatable island anchored near their dock. The water was crystal clear then — so clear that the kids could look down and see perch nipping at their toes beneath the surface.

Now, Cramer sinks past her ankles in slimy muck when she tries to walk out into the lake. Her floating dock rests on the dirt and is infested with bugs. The last time Cramer’s son and several of her grandchildren tried to swim in the water — about a year ago — they got sick. Cramer blames the worsening water quality and refuses to swim.

Cedar Lake, a moderately sized reservoir with an estimated storage capacity of 1,000 acre-feet, was created in the 1950s when the Western Sportsman Club dammed a tributary to the Canadian River in central Oklahoma, according to a surface water application obtained by the Caller and an Oklahoma Water Resources Board (OWRB) webpage.

Residents describe the gated lakeside community, located about 50 miles west of Oklahoma City, as small but tight-knit: only about 400 people lived there in 2020, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. Cramer appreciates the friendly neighborhood, where people help each other without expecting anything in return.

Yet now, many residents say the home they love is slowly being destroyed. According to pictures of Cramer’s dock taken in 2019 and 2026, Cedar Lake levels appear feet lower than they were seven years ago. Other images show docks feet away from the water. Some residents say their dried-up wells do not provide the water they need for everyday life.

Cramer’s Cedar Lake dock with an inflatable island in 2019

Residents like Cramer blame an unpermitted dam located on land managed by former Oklahoma Secretary of State Glenn Coffee.

Coffee has long been a prominent figure in Oklahoma politics. He served in the state Senate for 12 years before Republican Governor Mary Fallin named him Oklahoma secretary of state in 2011. Coffee began serving as senior advisor to the Oklahoma State Senate in 2025.

Now, some Cedar Lake residents blame “Coffee Dam No. 6” for their dwindling water supply, alleging the politically connected lawyer is retaining streamflow that should be reaching their community. (RELATED: Meet The ‘Rogue’ FBI Bureaucrat Who Said She Ran A ‘Shadow Government’)

A spokesperson for the OWRB, the state agency that oversees water rights, told the Caller the agency investigated the situation. In a summary of its findings, the OWRB pointed to drought, an overused aquifer and the Western Sportsman Club’s original assessment that streamflow would be insufficient to maintain Cedar Lake. The OWRB approved a consent order in September that requires Coffee to apply for permits for several dams — but does not resolve problems at Cedar Lake.

“Based on the investigation, OWRB staff is unable to determine that the lowered water levels in Cedar Lake are related to the construction of the upstream dams,” the OWRB told the Caller.

Hydrologist Carol Becker, who has worked with Oklahoma water systems for more than 35 years, reached a different conclusion. Her July report identified the two upstream dams as the primary cause of Cedar Lake’s declining water levels. The OWRB declined to comment when the Caller asked about this report.

Coffee also has longstanding ties to the OWRB. He served as counsel for the agency in two major water-rights cases settled in 2016, according to court documents. In 2006, while serving in the state Senate, Coffee also appointed current OWRB member Ron Justice as co-chair of the Senate Agriculture Committee.

Neither Coffee nor his attorney responded to multiple requests for comment.

The Caller spoke with nearly a dozen Cedar Lake residents and property owners, both on the record and on background, reviewed OWRB documents and consulted legal experts and hydrologists.

Cedar Lake resident Kacee Corey first noticed the lake level dropping about five years ago. She joked about it with friends — until the cove around her family’s dock dried up and filled with brush.

“[I]t just kept going down and down,” Corey said. “And now there’s just nothing but trees.”

Belinda Smith moved to a rental property near Cedar Lake three years ago, drawn to the quiet of the secluded community. But within months, the 70-year-old began finding sand in her water. Then her well went dry. Her landlord flushed the well in an attempt to restore the flow, but the water never returned.

Smith’s doctors have warned her not to exert herself, and she describes herself as “bent halfway over” from scoliosis. Hauling water supplied by a friend is difficult.

“It’s hard to pick up the five-gallon jug,” Smith said.

After her well went dry, Smith began dreading mornings, when she had to pour and heat water before carrying it to the bathroom or sink.

Smith is far from alone. Becker’s report included a May and June 2026 survey of Cedar Lake residents conducted online and through word of mouth. Erik Carlson’s Cedar Lake dock in 2019

Erik Carlson’s Cedar Lake dock in 2019. Carlson has sold his boat since the water level has decreased so much that he cannot use his dock.

Mirchi emphasized that prolonged droughts would exacerbate Cedar Lake’s situation. After reviewing an OWRB presentation, he also admitted the agency might be correct that reduced runoff is not the main cause of declining water levels.

But it might not be so simple.

That means Coffee’s dams could theoretically reduce the amount of water flowing toward Cedar Lake without violating the club’s rights, so long as the club still receives the amount to which it is legally entitled.

The OWRB also pointed to historical documents showing that the engineers who designed Cedar Lake doubted streamflow alone would be sufficient to maintain it.

“It is felt that the yield of the stream will not be sufficient to maintain a lake of the area and capacity required for their operation,” the engineers wrote, according to the OWRB’s summary.

“Evaporation losses outpace streamflow and runoff during drought years,” the agency’s summary report reads, especially because “backup groundwater supply to keep lake levels up has been abandoned.”

Kaylee Davis-Maddy, an attorney who has worked on Oklahoma water-law issues, said the OWRB would probably describe the state as the entity being harmed by Coffee’s unpermitted use of stream water. Stream water is a public resource under Oklahoma law, she explained.

Coffee’s application listed more than 500 potentially affected addresses, including addresses associated with Cedar Lake residents.

Residents like Corey say fears of losing access to water have forced them to ration what they have. In Becker’s survey, 44 percent of respondents who answered a question about water use said they relied on well water for all household needs, including cooking and bathing.

Smith still cannot run her washing machine and has resorted to camping showers because a $17 shower at a nearby truck stop is too expensive on her limited budget.

But Davis-Maddy noted that Oklahoma law treats groundwater and surface-water rights separately, which could make it difficult for residents to challenge Coffee’s surface-water use based on harm to their wells.

It does not require removal of Dam No. 6, instead citing the possibility of “flooding which Coffee Dam No. 6 now acts to contain.”

The OWRB told the Caller it had no documentation of dangerous flooding in the stream system before the dam was built.

She still takes her clothes to a laundromat because the tote does not provide enough pressure to run her washing machine.

The tank and pump trailer hooked up for Belinda Smith

“God’s good,” she said. “I believe He’ll help these people here because we sure need it.”

Cramer still cherishes memories of crystal-clear water and her grandchildren splashing in Cedar Lake. She fears those days may be gone for good.

“If they don’t make [Coffee] do right, it’s all going to be gone,” she said.

Coffee called then-Oklahoma Department of Corrections Director Justin Jones in 2011 to ask Jones to call House leaders and seek approval for a bill that would increase per-inmate rates for private prisons.

Some Cedar Lake residents believe Coffee’s efforts to retain his dams stem from corruption.

“I’m very disappointed. I’m a lifelong Oklahoman, and I’ve believed in our system. And I believe the OWRB has failed us,” Sullivan said. “It looks like that they were trying to cover for a rich, powerful, politically connected individual.”

“[It’s] definitely political and a money thing,” Corey said. “I’m curious, what else is there that he wants?”

For Cedar Lake residents, the falling water levels are deeply personal.

“It’s like another death,” Corey said.

She said her dreams of spending days on the lake with her children and grandchildren have faded. They rarely want to visit anymore, and when the kids tried to swim over the Fourth of July, they came out covered in sand.

Davis-Maddy said one option may be for Cedar Lake residents to seek additional surface-water rights from the OWRB.

But many residents say they do not know what to do next. Some have invested heavily in their properties but would consider leaving if water levels keep falling. Others, including Smith, cannot afford to leave — or hire a lawyer.

Neighbors recently connected a roughly 250-gallon water tote to Smith’s house, giving her a limited supply. The tote must be periodically refilled, and Smith uses the water sparingly. She still takes her clothes to a laundromat because the tote does not provide enough pressure to run her washing machine.

The tank and pump trailer hooked up for Belinda Smith

“God’s good,” she said. “I believe He’ll help these people here because we sure need it.”

Cramer still cherishes memories of crystal-clear water and her grandchildren splashing in Cedar Lake. She fears those days may be gone for good.

“If they don’t make [Coffee] do right, it’s all going to be gone,” she said.

news.originalContent:
Illustration by Daily Caller Staff.

The Daily Caller’s website was discreetly censored as “misinformation,” and now everyone involved is playing the blame game.

A reader recently tried to access the Daily Caller’s website on the public WiFi at the Burlington International Airport in Vermont, which is municipally run. When the user tried to open an article, the reader was abruptly shown a prompt blocking the website as “Contentious & Misinformation.”

Jeff Bartley, the Director of Innovation and Marketing at the airport, assured the Caller they “absolutely did not block” the website.

“We are certainly not in the business attempting to dictate what is and should be blocked as ‘contentious or misinformation,’” Bartley told the Caller.

After confirming the prompt, which Bartley assumed was a glitch, he urgently made calls to resolve the issue. (RELATED: Republicans Cozying Up With Democrats To Save Liberals’ Favorite Censorship Agency)

Bartley suggested the Caller reach out to Purple WiFi, the airport’s WiFi carrier. Purple WiFi is a British company that provides WiFi for businesses and public venues, including the Burlington International Airport.

Purple WiFi told the Caller that the content was likely blocked because of content settings selected either by the airport or imposed by their third-party content-filter service, DNSFilter.

“While the defined categories are part of DNSFilter’s service, and so we use these to help customers define what ‘levels’ of filtering to apply, we do not set the categories that DNSFilter applies to a specified domain,” the carrier said.

In response to the Caller’s inquiry, Purple WiFi said they moved to have the website “whitelisted” on the airport’s domain.

DNSFilter is an AI-powered content filtering service that allows customers to restrict or specify the type of content users can access. DNSFilter has some categories that automatically filter things like “Adult Content” or “Terrorism and Hate,” while customers “set their own content policies” to block additional content.

The Caller was blocked as part of the “Contentious & Misinformation” category, which needs to be enabled by the customer.

“We don’t make editorial judgments about individual news outlets,” DNSFilter told the Caller.

Although they claimed not to make “editorial judgments,” DNSFilter admitted that they grouped the Daily Caller as part of the “misinformation” category.

“We group millions and millions of domains into categories for ease of management, so yes, those are samples of hundreds of categories that customers can choose from,” DNSFilter told the Caller. “What each customer chooses to filter as their policy is their choice.”

Although DNSFilter doesn’t enable the content filter themselves, they appear to encourage their customers to do so.

“The category is defined as sites that are contentious, often causing argument or controversy, characterized by strong opposing arguments, as well as sites that spread or aid in the spreading of misinformation,” the website reads. “This category can have a negative impact on productivity, as well as company culture.” (RELATED: Supreme Court Takes Up Landmark Government Censorship Case)

Evan Swarztrauber, principal at the telecom and technology industry consulting firm CorePoint Strategies, called DNSFilter “problematic” for filtering websites like the Daily Caller.

“DNSFilter touts over 57,000 organizations as customers,” Swarztrauber told the Caller. “It recommends a ‘misinformation’ filter to customers on an opt-in basis and reports that about 20 percent of its user base has it enabled. Its customer base includes large public WiFi networks, enterprise environments, and transportation hubs.”

“It is problematic from a free-speech standpoint that this company is apparently censoring conservative news outlets for thousands of customers while encouraging others to apply that same filter.”

DNSFilter has previously come under fire for alleged censorship. A recent report from Blaze News claimed that DNSFilter censored not only them and the Caller, but also other outlets like The Federalist, RedState, and One America News Network.

Nathan Leamer, founder of tech policy firm Fixed Gear Strategies and former FCC advisor, detailed how censorship typically targets conservative outlets.

“Across the Internet stack there are a number of choke points where gatekeepers can use their power to silence voices they do not like; most often we see this at the social media level,” Nathan Leamer, founder of Fixed Gear Strategies, told the Caller. “But down the Internet stack this is an issue that must be mitigated.” (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: Legal Group Pushes For Transparency On USAID Involvement In Censorship During Biden Admin)

With all parties involved denying culpability and ultimately resolving the issue swiftly, it may be the case that the censorship was enabled at a lower level rather than a top-down corporate policy.

Preston Byrne, a free speech lawyer at Bryne & Storm, noted that UK businesses like Purple WiFi are “highly sensitive to political influence” given the lack of First Amendment or “jawboning” protections. Jawboning refers to informal attempts by government officials to strong-arm private companies into doing things like censoring speech, rather than using legal power or formal legislation.

Bryne also theorized that a potential culprit for the censorship could be a “rogue employee” rather than a top-down corporate policy.

“In my practice I have directly observed a handful of cases where private companies have formally blocked or deplatformed US-based companies because of those companies’ political orientation or their posture vis-à-vis UK content censorship,” Byrne told the Caller. “In this case, given the rapid remediation, we are more likely looking at a rogue employee than formal corporate policy action.”

This is hardly the first time outlets like the Caller have confronted censorship. In 2023, conservative outlets sued the State Department under former President Joe Biden for allegedly suppressing conservative speech online.

The joint lawsuit was filed by the Federalist, the Daily Wire, the New Civil Liberties Alliance (NCLA), and the state of Texas.

The State Department later settled the lawsuit in April 2026 and agreed to stop supporting the technology that censored conservatives.

news.originalContent:
امانوئل مکرون، رئیس‌جمهور فرانسه، در سفری اعلام نشده برای ابراز «همبستگی»، وارد ریاض شد. او نخستین رهبر غربی است که از زمان تشدید حملات حوثی‌های متحد ایران وارد عربستان سعودی شد و با محمد بن سلمان ولیعهد دیدار کرد.

این بخشی از سفر رئیس‌جمهور فرانسه به کشورهای خلیج فارس است که با هدف تأمین نفت و گازوئیل و کاهش قیمت‌ها پس از اعتراضات خشونت‌آمیز بر سر افزایش سرسام‌آور هزینه‌های زندگی در فرانسه صورت می‌گیرد.

آقای مکرون که با انتقادهای سنگینی در فرانسه روبه‌روست به خبرنگاران گفت که «در حال انجام وظیفه خود» است و در «محل مأموریت» حضور دارد.

در بیانیه‌ای که دفتر ریاست جمهوری فرانسه پیش از ورود آقای مکرون به عربستان سعودی منتشر کرد، آمده بود که هدف از این سفر، «نشان دادن همبستگی فرانسه با پادشاهی عربستان سعودی در مقابل حملات حوثی‌ها به خاک این کشور و همچنین ادامه تلاش‌ها برای تأمین و متنوع‌سازی منابع هیدروکربنی است.»

امانوئل مکرون پیش از ورود به عربستان در قطر بود و آنجا اعلام کرد که فرانسه پرسنل و تجهیزات به بندر ینبع که پایانه نفتی بسیار مهمی در عربستان است اعزام کرده است.

خبر ورود آقای مکرون در حالی اعلام شد که ساعاتی پیش خبرگزاری‌ها از انفجار و ستون دود در نزدیکی فرودگاه عدن خبر دادند و حوثی‌های یمن گفتند که به یک پایگاه نظامی عربستان سعودی در بندر عدن حمله کرده‌اند.

حوثی‌ها در شبکه‌های اجتماعی از قول سرتیپ یحیی سریع، سخنگوی نظامی‌شان، گفتند که اتاق عملیات قرارگاه بدر را با یک موشک بالستیک هدف حمله «دقیق و مستقیم» قرار داده‌اند.

شاهدان عینی از مشاهده دود درنزدیکی فرودگاه عدن خبر داده‌اند.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

در همین حال، حوثی‌ها گفتند که امروز، چهارشنبه، هیچ پهپادی به سمت شهر مقدس مدینه پرتاب نکرده‌اند و هیچ عملیات نظامی هم در خاک عربستان سعودی انجام نداده‌اند.

این اظهارات حوثی‌ها پیش از اعلام حمله به عدن و در تکذیب بیانیه ائتلاف به رهبری عربستان سعودی بود.

ائتلاف به رهبری عربستان سعودی که با حوثی‌های متحد ایران می‌جنگد، امروز گفت که پنج پهپاد را رهگیری کرده است؛ از جمله پهپادهایی در منطقه مدینه.

ترکی المالکی، سخنگوی ائتلاف، در شبکه اجتماعی ایکس نوشت: «چهار پهپاد که به سمت پادشاهی پرتاب شده بودند، رهگیری و منهدم شدند.» او در پیام دوم رهگیری‌ها در منطقه شرقی و مدینه را اعلام کرد.

آقای المالکی مشخص نکرد چه کسی مسئول پرتاب این پهپادها بوده است. حوثی‌ها این خبر را تکذیب کردند و یحیی سریع گفت که امروز هیچ‌گونه عملیاتی «در عمق» خاک عربستان سعودی انجام نشده است.

عربستان سعودی دائم زیر حملات حوثی‌هاست، از جمله حمله‌ به فرودگاه بین‌المللی ریاض که مرگبارترین حمله به آن کشور در سال‌های اخیر بوده است.

مدینه، محل دفن پیامبر اسلام، حضرت محمد، و محل مسجدالنبی، در کنار مکه یکی از مقدس‌ترین شهرهای اسلامی به شمار می‌رود. حوثی‌ها وعده داده‌اند که به این شهرها حمله نکنند.

حوثی‌ها بیشتر بخش‌های شمال و ساحل شرقی دریای سرخ را در کنترل دارند و قصد دارند با تصرف تعز و حرکت به سمت عدن، این دو شهر استراتژیک را از کنترل ائتلاف به رهبری عربستان خارج کنند. اگر عدن سقوط کند یمن در عمل به دو بخشی شرقی و غربی تقسیم می‌شود.

حوثی‌ها مدتی است که تعز را محاصره کرده‌اند.

در خیابان‌های شهر تعز زباله‌ها انباشته شده است و ساکنان در صف گاز هستند و شهر در محاصره با کمبود کالاهای اساسی دست‌وپنجه نرم می‌کند.

به‌دلیل شدت جنگ حوثی‌ها و نیروهای دولتی یمن، امکان انتقال زباله‌ها وجود ندارد در نتیجه در خیابان سوزانده می‌شوند.

حوثی‌ها اوایل ماه اکتبر، با مسدود کردن جاده اصلی منتهی به جنوب و بندر عدن، تعز را محاصره کردند.

این وضعیت باعث آوارگی گسترده و وخیم‌تر شدن بحران انسانی شده است.

سازمان‌های امدادرسان از کمبود گسترده سوخت، مواد غذایی، دارو و آب آشامیدنی سالم خبر داده‌اند. برنامه جهانی غذا هفته پیش گفت که ذخایر آرد گندم در این شهر تقریبا به پایان رسیده است.
